description:
FILED s530a (Opus agent, 2026-10-31) as the measured residue of #4000.  PRE-EXISTING (base 0fb05a79 gives the same).

perl blesses the REFERENT, so a FIRST bless is seen through every reference to it, including references taken before the bless.  PCL caches an ARRAY / CODE object's class on each container's box slot, and #4000 records a class on the referent itself only on a RE-bless into a different class -- so these stay wrong (perl 5.40.3 vs the s530a tree; probes scratch/s530a/pr/b1.pl rows 4 5 8 14 16 18 19, b2.pl rows 1-4 11-13 16-18, b6.pl):
    my $u = []; my @lu = ($u); bless $u, 'Q'; print ref $lu[0];          # perl Q, PCL ARRAY
    my $u2 = []; my $r2 = $u2; bless $u2, 'Q'; print ref $r2;            # perl Q, PCL ARRAY
    my $bb = []; my $bb2 = $bb; bless $bb, 'Q'; print blessed($bb2);     # perl Q, PCL undef
    sub mk { my @s = (1); bless \@s, 'Q'; return \@s } print ref mk();  # perl Q, PCL ARRAY  (a real constructor idiom)
    my @arr; my $ra = \@arr; my $rb = \@arr; bless $ra, 'Q'; print ref $rb;   # perl Q, PCL ARRAY
    sub nm {3} bless \&nm, 'Q'; print ref \&nm;                         # perl Q, PCL CODE
    { package Q; use overload '""' => sub {"Qobj"} } my $w = []; my @l = ($w); bless $w, 'Q'; print "$l[0]";   # perl Qobj, PCL ARRAY(0x..)

WHAT WAS MEASURED (do not retry as is): the full design -- every bless of an ARRAY / CODE referent writes a weak eq table keyed by the referent, and every class reader asks it first -- passes all of the rows above, but a weak SBCL hash-table lookup costs ~54 ns against ~3 ns for a strong one (scratch/s530a/wt.lisp, wt2.lisp: 3M lookups 0.163 s weak / 0.009 s strong; :synchronized nil does not help), and it sits on every method call and every ref() of an array / code reference: bench A/B (scratch/s530a/bench4000.log, BENCH_RT_B = the base runtime) methret-arr (an array-based object's method call) 0.0924 -> 0.1564 s (+69 %), refarr (ref of a blessed and a plain array ref) 0.0441 -> 0.2198 s (5x).  The hash-object rows (methret, ovlsub) did not move.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS: a "this referent was ever blessed" test that costs a type test, not a weak lookup -- the vector / function cannot carry a slot.  Candidates to MEASURE: (1) the compiler knows `bless \@NAME` / `bless \&NAME` (the named-referent spellings, b6's idiom) and could record those referents in a STRONG table owned by the variable's lifetime; (2) p-backslash of an array / code consulting the re-bless table only while it is non-empty (moves the cost to `\@a`, not to every ref()); (3) a per-array header object (PCL arrays are adjustable vectors -- an array-header struct would give the slot, a representation change).


=== DONE (s532d) ===
BUILT AS RULED (s532), cl/ only, emission IDENTICAL: every bless of an ARRAY / CODE / qr referent writes *p-rebless-stash* (%p-note-bless, both p-bless arms; replaces %p-note-rebless) and sets the defglobal *p-aggregate-blessed*; *p-reblessed* is set on a CHANGE of class -- against the box's cached class, or against the class the table already held (a copy taken before the first bless has a NIL cache).  THE UNBLESSED PATH: %p-first-bless-class (flag test, kind test, weak gethash) is asked only after every slot a reader consults is NIL -- %p-target-class's wrapper arm (the wrapper's and BOX's own slot NIL; a hit is cached into the wrapper) and raw arm (BOX's slot NIL; cached into BOX) via %p-first-bless-cache, p-ref's raw ARRAY / CODE arms for a value with no box, p-get-class's raw arm, and %pcl-invocant-class's raw-referent arm (an unblessed code ref stored in a hash value has no box).  Hashes and the blessed-cached fast path read nothing new.
PROBES (perl 5.40.3 -> base 06a4b8ba -> tree; scratch/s532d/pr/b1.pl 21 rows, b2.pl 18 rows in the s532d worktree): tree == perl on all 39; base wrong on 20 + 13 (the task's 7 rows, method call / blessed / isa / can / overload "" / ref through the OLD copy, a code object, a qr, a re-bless through a pre-bless copy in both directions, `ref []` in a loop with an array bless in the program).
GUARD: Pl/t/blessed-copy-01.t rows 9-10 (perl-probed), inverse-verified (fail on 06a4b8ba).  ir-spec 2.6: "The FIRST bless belongs to the referent too".
BENCH (the ruling's bar; tools/bench-exec.pl A = tree runtime, B = base 06a4b8ba runtime interleaved, best-of-5, heavy.sh s532d bench, 02:37-02:38, load 1.4-1.5; scratch/s532d/out/bench4061.log):
    row          perl     A(tree)  B(base)   A vs B
    methret      0.0868   0.1032   0.1038    -0.6 %   (within noise)
    json-rt      0.8656   1.1754   1.1918    -1.4 %   (within noise)
    moo-objs     0.0413   0.1904   0.2225    -14 %    (noise: hash objects, nothing of this on their path)
    mapmulti     0.6600   0.7735   0.7758    -0.3 %   (within noise)
  -> the four ruling rows did not move: the member STAYS.
  INFO rows (NOT in the tool -- a scratch copy, scratch/s532d/mkbench.pl; the array/code-object shapes the ruling's rows do not reach):
    methret-arr  0.0830   0.0889   0.0855    +4 %     (an array object's method call: the cached slot, one more `let`)
    refarr-x     0.0854   0.1954   0.0849    2.3x     (ref() of an UNBLESSED [] in a program that blessed one array: one weak gethash per call, ~55 ns)
    arrobj-new   0.1269   0.5513   0.2880    1.9x     (`bless [ $_[1] ], $_[0]` constructor in a loop: the weak puthash per bless)
  WHY THE WRITE COSTS: SBCL weak hash tables are SYNCHRONIZED (hash-table-synchronized-p T); scratch/s532d/wt.lisp: 1M fresh vectors, a puthash 0.247 s vs 0.026 s for the loop alone (~220 ns), the extra gethash (re-bless detection when the cache is NIL) +35 ns, a get miss 53 ns.  The ruling priced "one weak-table write per bless" -- it is ~220 ns, and array- and code-based objects (Path::Tiny) pay it per construction.  FLAGGED for the reviewing session: keep (correctness, the ruled design) or revert the runtime half of fc560940 (self-contained) and leave #4061 measured.
